notApplicable.hdt045: HDT is a rigid-bar test. ISO 75 ends at 0.2 % outer-fibre strain, which a bar reaches once its modulus falls to about 225 MPa, so an elastomer has no meaningful HDT and makers list it as N/A. A value an elastomer's sheet publishes is shown and never decides. Sintering filaments are left out too: the finished part is the sintered metal or ceramic.

items.text: Ketones such as acetone, methylethylketone (MEK) and cyclohexanone are partial solvents for thermoplastic polyurethane elastomers. Elastollan products are unsuitable for long-term use in these solvents. Methyl ethyl ketone: volume swelling 105 % / 110 % / 130 %, reduction of tensile strength 80 % / 80 % / 90 % (ester / C 85 A / ether); other short-chained aliphatic ketones such as acetone have a similar effect.
items.note: Columns: Elastollan standard ester grades (e.g. 500, 800), Elastollan C 85 A, Elastollan ether grades (e.g. 1100); each at 23 °C and 60 °C, resistance expressed as hours, days, weeks, months or years. items.text: Aliphatic alcohols, such as ethanol and isopropanol, cause swelling of Elastollan products. This is combined with a loss of tensile strength. Ethanol: volume swelling 16 % / 18 % / 33 %, reduction of tensile strength 52 % / 52 % / 64 % (ester / C 85 A / ether); after evaporation of the solvents the tensile strength recovers approximately its original value.
items.note: Columns: Elastollan standard ester grades (e.g. 500, 800), Elastollan C 85 A, Elastollan ether grades (e.g. 1100); each at 23 °C and 60 °C, resistance expressed as hours, days, weeks, months or years. items.text: Contact of Elastollan with aromatic hydrocarbons such as benzene and toluene results in considerable swelling even at room temperature. Absorption can result in a 50 % weight increase with a corresponding reduction in mechanical properties. Toluene: volume swelling 52 % / 60 % / 65 %, reduction of tensile strength 55 % / 45 % / 50 %.

items.agent: Lubricating oils and greases (IRM 901, 902, 903 test oils)
items.text: No reduction in strength occurs after immersion in test oils IRM 901, IRM 902, and IRM 903 at room temperature. There is also no reduction in tensile strength after 3 weeks immersion at 100 °C. Elastollan is in principal resistant to lubricating oils and greases, however irreversible damage can be caused by included additives. Compatibility testing in each individual lubricant is to be recommended.
items.conditions: Immersion at room temperature; 3 weeks at 100 °C

items.agent: Saturated hydrocarbons (diesel oil, isooctane, petroleum ether, kerosene)
items.text: Contact of Elastollan with saturated hydrocarbons such as diesel oil, isooctane, petroleum ether and kerosene results in a limited swelling. At room temperature, this swelling amounts to approx. 1-3 % and the resultant reduction in tensile strength is no more than 20 %. After evaporation and reversal of the swelling, the original mechanical properties are almost completely restored.

items.text: Plastics are chemically degraded by the effect of UV radiation. The degree of ageing depends on duration and intensity. In the case of polyurethanes, the effect is seen initially as surface embrittlement. This is accompanied by a yellowing in color and a reduction in mechanical properties. It is possible to improve UV resistance by addition of color pigments which prevent the deep penetration of UV rays... The ageing process can also be delayed by the addition of UV stabilizers.
